anchor.intro: {TIMECHECK} Welcome to GLC News. Ahead: Bill Gates warns A.I. could drive events that cause a billion deaths, the Trump administration's third-country deportations, Apple hit with a five point seven billion dollar haptic patent verdict, and Harry Kane scores again for England.
anchor.outro: Thanks Ernest for that report. That wraps this GLC News bulletin. Thank you for listening.

reporters.handoff: First, Edith on those third-country deportations.

stories.script: The Trump administration has deported more than twenty-five thousand people to at least twenty-eight countries even though those countries are not their own, the Washington Post reports. Coverage tied to France twenty-four and Forbidden Stories says migrants were sent to third countries under arrangements that stretch beyond traditional returns. Rights groups and legal advocates call the practice a sharp expansion of third-country removals.

reporters.signoff: I am Edith, for GLC News.

reporters.handoff: Thanks Edith. Mark with two tech stories, starting with Bill Gates.

stories.topic: Bill Gates on AI risk and regulation
stories.script: Bill Gates says artificial intelligence is certainly powerful enough to drive events that cause a billion deaths, and he is urging stronger government regulation beyond industry self-policing. In comments carried by N.B.C. Meet the Press, The Verge, and Business Insider, Gates argued that voluntary rules are not enough as the technology scales. He framed the risk as extreme enough that governments need clearer limits on how advanced systems are built and deployed.

A United States jury has ordered Apple to pay a record five point seven billion dollars after finding the company used patented haptic technology in iPhones and Apple Watches. Reuters, Bloomberg Law, and Law three sixty report the verdict as one of the largest patent awards against a tech giant. Apple is expected to appeal, while the plaintiffs say the win validates years of litigation over touch feedback patents.

reporters.signoff: I am Mark, for GLC News.

reporters.handoff: Thanks Mark. Ernest on Harry Kane.

stories.script: Harry Kane scored for England, lifting his tally to seven goals and eight goal contributions across club and country this season. Fabrizio Romano reported the strike live as England played. Kane remains England captain and continues to lead the line for Bayern Munich while stacking early-season numbers for club and country.

reporters.signoff: I am Ernest, for GLC News.
